claim: Cav1KO fibroblasts increase adhesion to FN-coated beads when pulled with magnetic tweezers, as compared to wild type fibroblasts.
source: Here, we show that Cav1KO fibroblasts increase adhesion to FN-coated beads when pulled with magnetic tweezers, as compared to wild type fibroblasts.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The increased adhesion phenotype in Cav1KO fibroblasts is Rho-independent.
source: This phenotype is Rho-independent and mainly derived from increased active β1-integrin content on the surface of Cav1KO fibroblasts.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 3C showing no effect of p190RhoGAP knockdown on reinforcement.

claim: Cav1KO fibroblasts have increased active β1-integrin content on their surface.
source: This phenotype is Rho-independent and mainly derived from increased active β1-integrin content on the surface of Cav1KO fibroblasts.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E-M.

claim: Active β1-integrin is mostly endocytosed through the clathrin independent carrier/glycosylphosphatidyl inositol (GPI)-enriched endocytic compartment pathway in Cav1KO fibroblasts.
source: Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching analysis and endocytosis/recycling assays revealed that active β1-integrin is mostly endocytosed through the clathrin independent carrier/glycosylphosphatidyl inositol (GPI)-enriched endocytic compartment pathway and is more rapidly recycled to the PM in Cav1KO fibroblasts, in a Rab4 and PM tension-dependent manner.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 5 showing ML141 inhibitor effects and dextran colocalization.

claim: Active β1-integrin is more rapidly recycled to the plasma membrane in Cav1KO fibroblasts in a Rab4 and PM tension-dependent manner.
source: Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching analysis and endocytosis/recycling assays revealed that active β1-integrin is mostly endocytosed through the clathrin independent carrier/glycosylphosphatidyl inositol (GPI)-enriched endocytic compartment pathway and is more rapidly recycled to the PM in Cav1KO fibroblasts, in a Rab4 and PM tension-dependent manner.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by recycling assay data in Figure 4G and I, and Rab4 dominant negative experiments in Figure 6.

claim: The threshold for PM tension-driven β1-integrin activation is lower in Cav1KO MEFs than in wild type MEFs.
source: Moreover, the threshold for PM tension-driven β1-integrin activation is lower in Cav1KO mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) than in wild type MEFs, through a mechanism dependent on talin activity.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by hypoosmotic shock experiments shown in Figure 7A-F.

claim: The mechanism of lower PM tension threshold for β1-integrin activation in Cav1KO MEFs is dependent on talin activity.
source: Moreover, the threshold for PM tension-driven β1-integrin activation is lower in Cav1KO mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) than in wild type MEFs, through a mechanism dependent on talin activity.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by talin knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7G-M.

claim: Caveolae couple mechanical stress to integrin cycling and activation.
source: Our findings suggest that caveolae couple mechanical stress to integrin cycling and activation, thereby regulating the early steps of the cellular mechanosensing response.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, inferred from the collective experimental findings presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Caveolae regulate the early steps of the cellular mechanosensing response.
source: Our findings suggest that caveolae couple mechanical stress to integrin cycling and activation, thereby regulating the early steps of the cellular mechanosensing response.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract as a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Integrins play an important role in cellular mechanosensing.
source: Cells are subjected to multiple mechanical inputs throughout their lives. Their ability to detect these environmental cues is called mechanosensing, a process in which integrins play an important role.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: Plasma membrane tension is adjusted to mechanical stress through the buffering action of caveolae during cellular mechanosensing.
source: During cellular mechanosensing, plasma membrane (PM) tension is adjusted to mechanical stress through the buffering action of caveolae; however, little is known about the role of caveolae in early integrin mechanosensing regulation.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and is supported by prior literature on caveolae function.

claim: Little is known about the role of caveolae in early integrin mechanosensing regulation.
source: During cellular mechanosensing, plasma membrane (PM) tension is adjusted to mechanical stress through the buffering action of caveolae; however, little is known about the role of caveolae in early integrin mechanosensing regulation.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and represents a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: Caveolae are present only in wild type MEFs and Cav1-reconstituted Cav1KO cells.
source: To validate the transgenic lines for the characterization of mechanosensing properties, we first analyzed the presence or absence of caveolae by electron microscopy (EM), detecting caveolae only in wild type (WT) and Cav1-reconstituted Cav1KO cells (Figure 1E–H, black arrows).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by electron microscopy images in Figure 1E-H.

claim: Re-expressed Cav1 localizes to the plasma membrane and does not form aberrant aggregates.
source: Next, super-resolution microscopy analysis of Cav1 topographical distribution revealed that re-expressed Cav1 localizes to the PM and does not form aberrant aggregates (Figure 1I–L).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by super-resolution microscopy images in Figure 1I-L.

claim: Biochemical fractionation indicated that re-expressed Cav1 localizes to the plasma membrane.
source: Confirming the super-resolution imaging data, biochemical fractionation indicated that re-expressed Cav1 localizes to the PM (Figure 1M).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by western blot data in Figure 1M.

claim: Cav1-reconstituted cells express near-endogenous levels of Cav1.
source: Western blot analysis confirmed the expected Cav1 and PTRF expression in the different MEF lines and revealed near-endogenous expression levels in Cav1-reconstituted cells (Figure 1N, see also Figure 1—source data 1–4).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by western blot data in Figure 1N.

claim: Reinforcement is significantly higher in Cav1KO MEFs exposed to FN-coated beads than in wild type MEFs.
source: Reinforcement was significantly higher in Cav1KO MEFs exposed to FN-coated beads than in wild type MEFs (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by quantitative data in Figure 2G.

claim: Reconstitution of Cav1KO MEFs with recombinant Cav1 rescued the wild type phenotype in reinforcement assays.
source: Reconstitution of Cav1KO MEFs with recombinant Cav1 rescued the WT phenotype, supporting that the Cav1KO phenotype is specific.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2G showing Cav1KO+Cav1 cells have similar reinforcement to wild type.

claim: Reconstitution of Cav1KO MEFs with PTRF induced a partial recovery in reinforcement that did not reach statistical significance.
source: Reconstitution of Cav1KO MEFs with PTRF induced a partial recovery that did not reach statistical significance.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2G.

claim: Magnetic tweezer pulling upon binding to ConA-coated beads yielded no significant differences in reinforcement across genotypes.
source: In contrast, MT pulling upon binding to ConA-coated beads yielded no significant differences across genotypes (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2H.

claim: FN-coated beads are surrounded by both phalloidin and 9EG7 signals, indicating engagement of both β1-integrin and the cell cytoskeleton.
source: Staining for phalloidin and 9EG7 antibody (which specifically recognizes β1-integrin in its active conformation; Lenter et al., 1993) revealed FN-coated beads surrounded by both signals, indicating engagement of both β1-integrin and the cell cytoskeleton; in contrast, ConA-coated beads were excluded from these stainings (Figure 2E and F), indicating they are only bound bulk PM, as previously reported (Gauthier et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by confocal microscopy images in Figure 2E and F.

claim: ConA-coated beads are excluded from phalloidin and 9EG7 staining, indicating they are only bound to bulk plasma membrane.
source: Staining for phalloidin and 9EG7 antibody (which specifically recognizes β1-integrin in its active conformation; Lenter et al., 1993) revealed FN-coated beads surrounded by both signals, indicating engagement of both β1-integrin and the cell cytoskeleton; in contrast, ConA-coated beads were excluded from these stainings (Figure 2E and F), indicating they are only bound bulk PM, as previously reported (Gauthier et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by confocal microscopy images in Figure 2E and F, with citation to prior work.

claim: 9EG7 antibody specifically recognizes β1-integrin in its active conformation.
source: Staining for phalloidin and 9EG7 antibody (which specifically recognizes β1-integrin in its active conformation; Lenter et al., 1993) revealed FN-coated beads surrounded by both signals, indicating engagement of both β1-integrin and the cell cytoskeleton
evidence: This claim is stated in the text with a citation to Lenter et al., 1993.

claim: Cav1 regulates cell contraction by controlling Rho activity through the localization of p190RhoGAP.
source: We previously showed that Cav1 regulates cell contraction by controlling Rho activity through the localization of p190RhoGAP (Grande-García et al., 2007) within the PM (Grande-García et al., 2007; Goetz et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text with citations to prior work by the authors.

claim: In the absence of Cav1, p190RhoGAP localization to liquid order domains increases, where it can bind and inhibit Rho activity.
source: In the absence of Cav1, p190RhoGAP localization to liquid order domains increases, where it can bind and inhibit Rho activity (Goetz et al., 2011), thus attenuating cell contractility and associated ECM remodeling (Grande-García et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Reduced cell contractility in Cav1KO cells contrasts with the local stiffening response observed in magnetic tweezer assays.
source: This reduced cell contractility contrasts with the local stiffening response observed in our MT assays.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text as an observation comparing two different experimental outcomes.

claim: Specific knock down of p190RhoGAP fully rescues other biomechanical phenotypes in Cav1KO MEFs.
source: Because the specific knock down of this p190RhoGAP isoform fully rescues other biomechanical phenotypes in Cav1KO MEFs (Gauthier et al., 2011; Grande-García et al., 2007), we assessed the impact of stably knocking down p190RhoGAP (Goetz et al., 2011) on the increased reinforcement observed in Cav1KO cells
evidence: This claim is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Traction force microscopy confirmed higher overall contractility in p190RhoGAP-depleted Cav1KO MEFs.
source: While traction force microscopy confirmed higher overall contractility in p190RhoGAP-depleted Cav1KO MEFs as expected (Goetz et al., 2011; Figure 3D), MT measurements revealed no decreased reinforcement upon p190RhoGAP knockdown (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by traction force microscopy data in Figure 3D.

claim: Magnetic tweezer measurements revealed no decreased reinforcement upon p190RhoGAP knockdown in Cav1KO MEFs.
source: While traction force microscopy confirmed higher overall contractility in p190RhoGAP-depleted Cav1KO MEFs as expected (Goetz et al., 2011; Figure 3D), MT measurements revealed no decreased reinforcement upon p190RhoGAP knockdown (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by magnetic tweezer data in Figure 3C.

claim: Cav1KO MEFs locally respond to FN-coated beads in a Rho-independent manner.
source: These observations suggest that Cav1KO MEFs locally respond to FN-coated beads in a Rho-independent manner, as opposed to Rho-dependent whole cell contractility.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text as a conclusion drawn from the p190RhoGAP knockdown experiments.

claim: Adhesion to ConA-coated plates did not differ between genotypes.
source: Whereas adhesion to ConA-coated plates did not differ between genotypes (Figure 3E), adhesion to FN was higher in Cav1KO MEFs and PTRF-reconstituted Cav1KO MEFs (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by adhesion assay data in Figure 3E.

claim: Adhesion to FN was higher in Cav1KO MEFs and PTRF-reconstituted Cav1KO MEFs.
source: Whereas adhesion to ConA-coated plates did not differ between genotypes (Figure 3E), adhesion to FN was higher in Cav1KO MEFs and PTRF-reconstituted Cav1KO MEFs (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by adhesion assay data in Figure 3F.

claim: Cav1 re-expression rescued the wild type phenotype in FN adhesion assays.
source: Cav1 re-expression rescued the wild type phenotype, supporting a specific role of Cav1 in cellular adhesion.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by adhesion assay data in Figure 3F.

claim: PTRF reconstitution did not have a significant impact on Cav1KO MEFs adhesion.
source: However, PTRF reconstitution did not have a significant impact on Cav1KO MEFs adhesion and was therefore not considered further in subsequent experiments.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by adhesion assay data in Figure 3F.

claim: Cav1KO MEFs showed always higher adhesion than wild type MEFs in experiments with different FN concentrations and other integrin-dependent coatings (collagen and vitronectin).
source: In additional experiments with different FN concentrations and other integrin-dependent coatings (collagen and vitronectin), Cav1KO MEFs showed always higher adhesion than wild type MEFs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C and D).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by adhesion assay data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C and D.

claim: The two major FN receptors are integrins α5β1 and αvβ3.
source: The two major FN receptors are integrins α5β1 and αvβ3 (Plow et al., 2000); however, adhesion strength is mainly mediated by the clustering and activation (Friedland et al., 2009; Lin et al., 2013) of integrin α5β1.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text with a citation to prior work.

claim: Adhesion strength is mainly mediated by the clustering and activation of integrin α5β1.
source: The two major FN receptors are integrins α5β1 and αvβ3 (Plow et al., 2000); however, adhesion strength is mainly mediated by the clustering and activation (Friedland et al., 2009; Lin et al., 2013) of integrin α5β1.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: The active β1-integrin signal was consistently stronger in Cav1KO MEFs than in wild type MEFs over a range of conditions.
source: The active β1-integrin signal was consistently stronger in Cav1KO MEFs than in wild type MEFs over a range of conditions: permeabilized and non-permeabilized cells, around FN-coated beads and at different spreading time points (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–M).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by immunostaining data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E-M.

claim: Cav1KO MEFs displayed stronger FN adhesion than wild type MEFs, a phenotype presumably derived from increased active β1-integrin at the cell surface.
source: Cav1KO MEFs displayed stronger FN adhesion than wild type MEFs, a phenotype presumably derived from increased active β1-integrin at the cell surface.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text as a conclusion drawn from the adhesion and immunostaining data.

claim: Experiments measuring fluorescence recovery after photobleaching in Cav1KO and wild type MEFs revealed no significant differences in fluorescence recovery between the two cell populations.
source: However, experiments measuring fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) in Cav1KO and wild type MEFs expressing similar levels of GFP-fused β1-integrin (Figure 4A, B) revealed no significant differences in fluorescence recovery between the two cell populations, indicating that lateral mobility of β1-integrin was unaffected (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by FRAP data in Figure 4C.

claim: Lateral mobility of β1-integrin was unaffected in Cav1KO MEFs compared to wild type MEFs.
source: However, experiments measuring fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) in Cav1KO and wild type MEFs expressing similar levels of GFP-fused β1-integrin (Figure 4A, B) revealed no significant differences in fluorescence recovery between the two cell populations, indicating that lateral mobility of β1-integrin was unaffected (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by FRAP data in Figure 4C.

claim: β1-integrins in wild type MEFs are stable, largely immobile structures as revealed by TIRF videos.
source: Total Internal Reflection Fluorescence (TIRF) videos revealed β1-integrins in wild type MEFs as stable, largely immobile structures; in contrast, β1-integrins in Cav1KO MEFs showed a dynamic behavior, rapidly appearing and disappearing from the PM plane (Figure 4—videos 1 and 2 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and 1B).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by TIRF microscopy videos and images in Figure 4—videos 1 and 2 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and 1B.

claim: β1-integrins in Cav1KO MEFs showed a dynamic behavior, rapidly appearing and disappearing from the plasma membrane plane.
source: Total Internal Reflection Fluorescence (TIRF) videos revealed β1-integrins in wild type MEFs as stable, largely immobile structures; in contrast, β1-integrins in Cav1KO MEFs showed a dynamic behavior, rapidly appearing and disappearing from the PM plane (Figure 4—videos 1 and 2 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and 1B).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by TIRF microscopy videos and images in Figure 4—videos 1 and 2 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and 1B.

claim: Integrins increased their dynamicity after treatment with high hypoosmotic pressure in wild type MEFs, mimicking Cav1KO phenotype.
source: Interestingly, integrins increased their dynamicity after treatment with high hypoosmotic pressure in wild type MEFs, mimicking Cav1KO phenotype (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–F, and Figure 4—videos 3–6, quantified in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F, see Materials and methods for more details), suggesting that PM tension changes could affect integrin trafficking dynamics.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by TIRF microscopy data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C-F.

claim: PM tension changes could affect integrin trafficking dynamics.
source: Interestingly, integrins increased their dynamicity after treatment with high hypoosmotic pressure in wild type MEFs, mimicking Cav1KO phenotype (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–F, and Figure 4—videos 3–6, quantified in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F, see Materials and methods for more details), suggesting that PM tension changes could affect integrin trafficking dynamics.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text as a suggestion based on the hypoosmotic treatment experiments.

claim: In adherent cells, integrins undergo constant endocytic-exocytic shuttling to facilitate the dynamic regulation of cell adhesion.
source: In adherent cells, integrins undergo constant endocytic-exocytic shuttling to facilitate the dynamic regulation of cell adhesion (Bretscher and Aguado-Velasco, 1998).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text with a citation to prior work.

claim: Cav1KO and wild type MEFs showed no significant differences in endocytic rates of total and active β1-integrin at early time points (2, 5, and 10 min) during early spreading.
source: We first analyzed the endocytic rates of total and active β1-integrin at early time points (2, 5, and 10 min) during early spreading (2 hr after seeding), to recapitulate the conditions used in MT experiments (see Materials and methods for details). Cav1KO and wild type MEFs showed no significant differences, indicating that β1 endocytosis is Cav1-independent at these early time points (Figure 4F and H).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by endocytosis assay data in Figure 4F and H.

claim: β1 endocytosis is Cav1-independent at early time points (2, 5, and 10 min).
source: Cav1KO and wild type MEFs showed no significant differences, indicating that β1 endocytosis is Cav1-independent at these early time points (Figure 4F and H).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by endocytosis assay data in Figure 4F and H.

claim: After 5 min of endocytosis, wild type and Cav1KO MEFs showed no major differences in total β1-integrin recycling rates.
source: After 5 min of endocytosis, wild type and Cav1KO MEFs showed no major differences in total β1-integrin recycling rates at either time point set (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G, H).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by recycling assay data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1G, H.

claim: After 10 min endocytosis, Cav1KO MEFs recycled total and active β1-integrin faster than wild type MEFs in the 1-3-5 min recycling set.
source: In contrast, after 10 min endocytosis, Cav1KO MEFs recycled total and active β1-integrin faster than wild type MEFs in the 1-3-5 min recycling set (Figure 4G and I).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by recycling assay data in Figure 4G and I.

claim: Reconstitution of Cav1KO MEFs with recombinant Cav1 rescued active β1-integrin recycling but not total β1-integrin.
source: Importantly, reconstitution of Cav1KO MEFs with recombinant Cav1 rescued active β1-integrin recycling but not total β1-integrin, supporting that the Cav1KO phenotype is specific at least for the active pool (Figure 4—figure supplement 1I, J).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by recycling assay data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1I, J.

claim: β1-integrin is stabilized in the presence of Cav1 after 10 min endocytosis.
source: These results suggest that β1-integrin is stabilized in the presence of Cav1 after 10 min endocytosis, whereas in Cav1KO MEFs its shuttling to PM is accelerated, increasing its surface availability and thus enhancing adhesion to FN-coated beads and reinforcement response.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text as a conclusion drawn from the recycling assay data.

claim: In Cav1KO MEFs, β1-integrin shuttling to plasma membrane is accelerated, increasing its surface availability and thus enhancing adhesion to FN-coated beads and reinforcement response.
source: These results suggest that β1-integrin is stabilized in the presence of Cav1 after 10 min endocytosis, whereas in Cav1KO MEFs its shuttling to PM is accelerated, increasing its surface availability and thus enhancing adhesion to FN-coated beads and reinforcement response.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text as a conclusion drawn from the recycling assay data.

claim: Recent work showed increased exocytosis after loading wild type MEFs with cholesterol, phenocopying Cav1KO MEFs where cholesterol accrued in different endosomal compartments.
source: Different mechanisms could account for this stabilization; however, recent work in our lab showed increased exocytosis after loading wild type MEFs with cholesterol, phenocopying Cav1KO MEFs where cholesterol accrued in different endosomal compartments (Albacete-Albacete et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text with a citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Treatment of wild type MEFs with U18666A or LDLs induced a significant increase in surface active β1-integrin.
source: Interestingly, both treatments induced a significant increase in surface active β1-integrin (Figure 4—figure supplement 1K) that was also accompanied by an increased colocalization with EEA-1 positive endosomes in LDL-treated cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1L–N).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1K.

claim: LDL treatment of wild type MEFs was accompanied by increased colocalization of β1-integrin with EEA-1 positive endosomes.
source: Interestingly, both treatments induced a significant increase in surface active β1-integrin (Figure 4—figure supplement 1K) that was also accompanied by an increased colocalization with EEA-1 positive endosomes in LDL-treated cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1L–N).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by colocalization data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1L-N.

claim: There might be a Cav1-dependent cholesterol threshold above which β1-integrin trafficking is altered, phenocopying Cav1KO MEFs where both surface and intracellular active β1-integrin levels are increased.
source: These results might be indicative of a Cav1-dependent cholesterol threshold above which β1-integrin trafficking is altered, phenocopying Cav1KO MEFs where both surface and intracellular active β1-integrin levels are increased.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text as a speculative interpretation of the cholesterol loading experiments.

claim: β1-integrin endocytosis has been suggested to be Cav1-dependent in different systems.
source: β1-integrin endocytosis has been suggested to be Cav1-dependent in different systems (Shi and Sottile, 2008; Du et al., 2011); however, we observed no differences between Cav1KO and wild type MEFs in net β1-integrin endocytosis.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: The CLIC/GEEC endocytic route is negatively regulated by caveolar proteins, including Cav1 and PTRF.
source: To investigate how Cav1KO MEFs achieve similar levels of β1-integrin endocytosis as wild type MEFs, we decided to analyze endocytosis via clathrin independent carriers (CLICs), especially because this endocytic modality is negatively regulated by caveolar proteins, including Cav1 and PTRF (Chaudhary et al., 2014; Cheng et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: The CLIC/GEEC endocytic route accounts for ~threefold internalized volume as compared to clathrin-mediated endocytosis in fibroblasts.
source: Furthermore, this endocytic route is highly relevant for fibroblast trafficking dynamics—accounting for ~threefold internalized volume as compared to clathrin-mediated endocytosis—and β1-integrin is a specific cargo (Howes et al., 2010; Lakshminarayan et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: β1-integrin is a specific cargo of the CLIC/GEEC endocytic route.
source: Furthermore, this endocytic route is highly relevant for fibroblast trafficking dynamics—accounting for ~threefold internalized volume as compared to clathrin-mediated endocytosis—and β1-integrin is a specific cargo (Howes et al., 2010; Lakshminarayan et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Cells lacking Cav1 increase CLIC endocytosis through the small GTPase Cdc42 activation.
source: Interestingly, cells lacking Cav1 increase CLIC endocytosis through the small GTPase Cdc42 activation (Cheng et al., 2010), which is known to regulate this endocytic pathway (Mayor et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Cdc42 is known to regulate the CLIC/GEEC endocytic pathway.
source: Interestingly, cells lacking Cav1 increase CLIC endocytosis through the small GTPase Cdc42 activation (Cheng et al., 2010), which is known to regulate this endocytic pathway (Mayor et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text with a citation to prior work.

claim: ML141 significantly reduced β1-integrin endocytosis in Cav1KO MEFs, whereas wild type MEFs were unaffected.
source: ML141 significantly reduced β1-integrin endocytosis in Cav1KO MEFs, whereas wild type MEFs were unaffected (Figure 5A and B), indicating that β1-integrin is partially endocytosed through the CLIC/GEEC pathway in Cav1KO MEFs.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by endocytosis assay data in Figure 5A and B.

claim: β1-integrin is partially endocytosed through the CLIC/GEEC pathway in Cav1KO MEFs.
source: ML141 significantly reduced β1-integrin endocytosis in Cav1KO MEFs, whereas wild type MEFs were unaffected (Figure 5A and B), indicating that β1-integrin is partially endocytosed through the CLIC/GEEC pathway in Cav1KO MEFs.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by ML141 inhibitor experiments in Figure 5A and B.

claim: Cav1KO MEFs displayed significantly higher uptake of the fluid-phase endocytosis marker dextran as compared to wild type cells.
source: In accordance with this finding, Cav1KO MEFs displayed significantly higher uptake of the fluid-phase endocytosis marker dextran (Sabharanjak et al., 2002), as well as elevated colocalization of dextran and Alexa-488-labeled β1-integrin (Figure 5C–H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1), as compared to wild type cells.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by dextran uptake data in Figure 5C-H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cav1KO MEFs displayed elevated colocalization of dextran and Alexa-488-labeled β1-integrin as compared to wild type cells.
source: In accordance with this finding, Cav1KO MEFs displayed significantly higher uptake of the fluid-phase endocytosis marker dextran (Sabharanjak et al., 2002), as well as elevated colocalization of dextran and Alexa-488-labeled β1-integrin (Figure 5C–H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1), as compared to wild type cells.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by colocalization data in Figure 5C-H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the absence of Cav1, early endocytosis of β1-integrin occurs at least in part through CLIC uptake, which provides an alternative entry route that would compensate for lack of Cav1-dependent internalization.
source: Thus, in the absence of Cav1, early endocytosis of β1-integrin occurs at least in part through CLIC uptake, which provides an alternative entry route that would compensate for lack of Cav1-dependent internalization.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text as a conclusion drawn from the CLIC endocytosis experiments.

claim: β1-integrin endocytosis was mainly Cav1-dependent in wild type MEFs as it colocalized with Cav1 and LacCer.
source: Consistent with previous results, β1-integrin endocytosis was mainly Cav1-dependent in wild type MEFs as it: (i) colocalized with Cav1 and LacCer, (ii) was significantly reduced upon genistein treatment (a caveolar endocytosis inhibitor Rejman et al., 2005), and (iii) was unaffected by ML141 treatment (the CLIC inhibitor; Figure 5—figure supplement 1D–K).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by colocalization and inhibitor data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-K.

claim: β1-integrin endocytosis in wild type MEFs was significantly reduced upon genistein treatment.
source: Consistent with previous results, β1-integrin endocytosis was mainly Cav1-dependent in wild type MEFs as it: (i) colocalized with Cav1 and LacCer, (ii) was significantly reduced upon genistein treatment (a caveolar endocytosis inhibitor Rejman et al., 2005), and (iii) was unaffected by ML141 treatment (the CLIC inhibitor; Figure 5—figure supplement 1D–K).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by genistein treatment data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-K.

claim: β1-integrin endocytosis in wild type MEFs was unaffected by ML141 treatment.
source: Consistent with previous results, β1-integrin endocytosis was mainly Cav1-dependent in wild type MEFs as it: (i) colocalized with Cav1 and LacCer, (ii) was significantly reduced upon genistein treatment (a caveolar endocytosis inhibitor Rejman et al., 2005), and (iii) was unaffected by ML141 treatment (the CLIC inhibitor; Figure 5—figure supplement 1D–K).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by ML141 treatment data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-K.

claim: β1-integrin endocytosis was mainly CLIC-dependent in Cav1KO MEFs as it colocalized with CD44.
source: On the other hand, β1-integrin endocytosis was mainly CLIC-dependent in Cav1KO MEFs as it: (i) colocalized with CD44 and (ii) was significantly reduced upon ML141 treatment as compared to wild type MEFs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1L–P).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by colocalization data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1L-P.

claim: β1-integrin endocytosis in Cav1KO MEFs was significantly reduced upon ML141 treatment as compared to wild type MEFs.
source: On the other hand, β1-integrin endocytosis was mainly CLIC-dependent in Cav1KO MEFs as it: (i) colocalized with CD44 and (ii) was significantly reduced upon ML141 treatment as compared to wild type MEFs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1L–P).
